Wait, let me re-read carefully. "Queens may not touch, including diagonally. Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." This is the standard non-touching rule for adjacent rows.
    *   **Crucial Exception:** "Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." This means if I have a queen at (1, 1) and another at (3, 3), that's allowed. The constraint is only for *consecutive* rows. So, if row $i$ has a queen at col $c_i$ and row $i+1$ has a queen at col $c_{i+1}$, then $|c_i - c_{i+1}| \neq 1$.
